name: Gareth Arrieta
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “Night nursing taught me which breakfast places keep the lights low.” Sunday often includes a stop at Juniper Street, where Gareth knows which of the west-side porches has a seat in the shade.
voice: I listen for the doors before putting toast down. Now I burn it every morning and blame the council.
appearance: Gareth has fine brows over wide-set eyes. Look for short, uneven waves that refuse to lie flat. Out of work clothes, the familiar outfit is a cropped bottle-green coat with one loose pocket corner secured with green thread. In conversation Gareth looks toward the door whenever a name is called.
personality: Gareth tells a better story in a kitchen than at a microphone. Family members sometimes underestimate how far Gareth will go to back a quiet opinion once it is actually challenged.
agenda: To get toast and shift time back into sensible order.
family: Daryl Akers is Gareth’s half-sibling. Gareth saves a place. Daryl chooses whether to use it. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *The clean ledger*, Daryl says, “I learned to read in prison. My own name on that page was the first word I didn't want to see.”
connections: Ada Ellis. They trade better directions for the warning sound that once timed the morning toast.

reactions.response: Gareth asks one rider from each corner to walk the new distance.

reactions.response: Gareth looks for a second safe place to sit and stays long enough for the waiting people to settle.
